title: review: S1b: skill telemetry in shadow: which skills each worker was exposed to and invoked, skill tokens per run, skill_selection decision rows, skill columns in the economy scorecard; exposure unchanged (v3)
spec:
Program brief .orchestrator/roadmap-skills.md P0 telemetry, P29, P30 (P37 stage 1). Depends on S1a T-0863 (orchestrator/skills_registry.py: SkillRecord, sync, registry records with roles/est tokens). Facts: Claude workers run in worktrees that carry .claude/skills (11 symlinked skills; all descriptions are in context, bodies load on Skill-tool invocation); Codex executors load implement-spec via AGENTS.md and their final message says "Skill used: <name>" when they did; bus.log_run rows carry packet_meta and a context object (P1 telemetry); decision_log.KINDS has the context-program kinds; context_scorecard builds per role/goal/task_class rows and `scorecard --economy` joins sources.
Do:
1. Exposure: in spawn.run_worker (and the Claude execute fallback) compute `skills_exposed` = registry records whose roles include the worker's role or "*" and whose state is active (today: all 11 for Claude roles; implement-spec for codex_execute via AGENTS.md), with skill_tokens_l0 = sum est_tokens_l0; write them into the task's packet_meta ("skills_exposed": ids, "skill_tokens_l0") so bus.log_run carries them into the run context (add the keys to bus.py's copied list). Codex dispatch (daemon/executor.start) records ["executor/implement-spec"] and its l0 tokens the same way.
2. Usage: after a worker finishes, detect invoked skills: for Claude workers parse the run transcript (the path recorded for the run; the executor verifies the exact JSON shape of a Skill tool_use in .orchestrator/runs transcripts and documents it) for tool_use names "Skill" with input.skill or the skill name; for Codex parse the result summary for "Skill used: <name>" lines. Record `skills_used` (ids), `skill_tokens_l2` (sum est_tokens_l2 of used skills) in the run row's context and in the task pipeline ("skills_used").
3. decision_log: add kind "skill_selection" to KINDS (and CONTEXT_KINDS docstring mapping); record one row per worker spawn: candidates = all registry ids for the role, hard_constraints = ["static exposure (stage 1)"], deterministic = {"role", "task_class", "exposed": ids, "skill_tokens_l0"}, selected = exposed ids, reason = "stage1 static", mode = "shadow"; and after completion decision_log.outcome(task, "skill_selection", skills_used=..., skill_tokens_l2=...).
4. Scorecard (P30 first metrics): orchestrator/skill_scorecard.py (new): from run rows: per role and per skill id: exposures, uses, use_rate, skill_tokens_l0 avg, skill_tokens_l2 avg, skill_overhead_ratio = (skill_tokens_l0 + skill_tokens_l2) / input tokens of the run (when input tokens known), plus per accepted task (lineage merged) skill_tokens_per_accepted_task. `orchestrator scorecard --skills` prints it; `scorecard --economy` gains a skills block.
5. docs/skill-intelligence/02-telemetry.md (≤60 lines): fields, where they live, how usage is detected for each worker kind, limits (Claude Code loads descriptions itself; l0 tokens are an estimate), revert path (nothing to revert: pure logging; remove the keys).
Constraints: no change to prompts, allowlists, symlinks or which skills a worker sees; a telemetry failure never breaks a spawn (try/except + one notify line). Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_spawn.py::test_run_worker_records_skills_exposed_and_l0_tokens, ::test_skill_usage_from_gate_rows_for_claude_workers, ::test_skill_usage_parsed_from_codex_summary; tests/test_bus.py::test_log_run_carries_skill_keys; tests/test_decision_log.py::test_skill_selection_kind_records_and_outcome; tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_use_rate_and_overhead_ratio_per_skill, ::test_skill_tokens_per_accepted_task.
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-23 01:50) after spec review T-0872 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- Session handle: spawn.run_claude reads `session_id` from the CLI's JSON result (`--output-format json`; the executor verifies the field name from a real run row or the CLI docs and records what it found) and stores it on the run row (bus.log_run field session_id) and on the task's packet_meta; when absent, session_id is None and Claude-side usage detection is best-effort.
- Usage detection for Claude workers uses two sources, no transcript parsing required: (1) the Jev gate log (.orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl, one row per gated tool call keyed by ORCH_TASK_ID / session): a Read of skills/<role>/<name>/SKILL.md or a Bash call of skills/<role>/<name>/scripts/* counts as a use of that skill; (2) jev_gate.run records Skill tool invocations too: when tool_name == "Skill" it logs {"tool": "Skill", "skill": input.skill or input.name} without asking Jev and without ever blocking (should_skip stays true for Skill after logging). orchestrator/jev_gate.py joins the scope for that one logging branch; tests/test_jev_gate.py gains ::test_skill_tool_invocation_is_logged_not_gated. Transcript parsing is descoped; if a transcript path is derivable from session_id (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…), document it in 02-telemetry.md as a future source only.
- decision_log: "skill_selection" is added to KINDS with a docstring line stating it has no legacy synonym (no invented pairing).

SPEC v3 (2026-09-23 02:20) after spec review T-0893 (round 2; points folded in, further review waived by the Planner, verdict set to approve):
- skills_exposed for Claude workers = every active registry record with provenance builtin (today all 11 symlinked skills; implement-spec is not symlinked and is exposed to Codex only), because exposure is the shared .claude/skills directory, not the per-role tags; the roles field stays informational for routing. For Codex executors skills_exposed = ["executor/implement-spec"].
- Skill-tool invocation logging is descoped: .claude/settings.json (the hook matcher) is a protected path outside any executor's scope, so jev_gate never sees Skill calls today. Usage detection relies on gate rows only (Read of skills/<role>/<name>/SKILL.md, Bash of skills/<role>/<name>/scripts/*) plus the Codex "Skill used:" summary line. orchestrator/jev_gate.py and tests/test_jev_gate.py leave the scope; the acceptance line for test_skill_tool_invocation_is_logged_not_gated is dropped. docs/skill-intelligence/02-telemetry.md states that Skill-tool invocations by Claude workers are not observable until the human adds "Skill" to the jev-gate PreToolUse matcher in .claude/settings.json (one-line change, recorded as a human item).
- decision_log: "skill_selection" is appended to CONTEXT_KINDS (which flows into KINDS), with the docstring line saying it has no legacy synonym.
acceptance: docs/skill-intelligence/02-telemetry.md exists; `uv run orchestrator scorecard --skills` runs; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

result.summary: Core Claude-side usage detection is broken: spawn._skills_from_gate reads a gate-log field that jev_gate.py never writes, so skills_used will always be empty in production even though its unit test passes.

comments.issue: _skills_from_gate reads row.get("input") to detect Read of SKILL.md / Bash of scripts/*, but jev_gate.py's _log() (the only writer of runs/jev/gate.jsonl) never emits an "input" key — it writes "tool_target" (a redacted path/command string) and "input_hash". orchestrator/read_economy.py, which reads the same log, correctly uses row.get("tool_target"). Because raw is always "", the substring checks against SKILL.md/scripts/ can never match, so skills_used/skill_tokens_l2 for Claude workers will always be empty in real runs, defeating the acceptance criterion this ships to satisfy. tests/test_spawn.py::test_skill_usage_from_gate_rows_for_claude_workers passes only because it fabricates a row with a nonstandard "input" key that real gate rows never contain.
STATE is added to the import list (`from . import ROOT, STATE, bus`) but never referenced anywhere in the file — dead import.
